analysis.title: The market is breaking out but something is wrong
key_insights: NDX is up roughly 7% since the Sep 10 note and is breaking above its final resistance into 'pure vacuum' territory. The 50-day moving average has turned positively sloped again.
NDX has gone essentially nowhere since May and is only now breaking out of a large consolidation. Bearishness intensified over the past few weeks inside that range.
BTIG says SOX continues to track the 2000 analog closely and is roughly where the sector was around the March 2000 peak. The analog points to choppy consolidation first, not an immediate crash.
With VXN more reasonably priced than in the summer and earnings approaching, vols are unlikely to ease much further. The suggested risk management is to switch from outright delta into call spreads.

Carlyle argues the first phase of the AI boom, financed by hyperscaler cash flows, is ending. Operating cash flow no longer covers intended spending, and more than 80% of anticipated AI capex through 2030 will need external financing via equity, debt and off-balance-sheet structures.
AI-related market financing is expected to exceed $500bn in 2026, more than double last year's total. Carlyle frames AI as moving from an earnings story to a capital-markets story.

Carlyle estimates US corporate net savings are down 86% relative to the same point in the previous cycle. Hyperscalers have moved from providers of liquidity to users of it, which bears on the rates outlook.

GS notes AI is absorbing large amounts of capital, depends increasingly on external financing and may contribute to structurally higher real rates, while a narrow group of AI-linked companies drives index earnings.
SPX is near its highs around 7,700, but Goldman's S&P ex-AI basket fell from roughly 3,300 in August to around 3,075.
Hedge funds bought TMT in September while nearly every other sector was sold. The top 10 stocks are expected to generate more than two-thirds of aggregate S&P 500 earnings growth this quarter.
Bond vol has kept rising even though the 10-year has made little progress over recent sessions. A reversal lower in rates could be amplified if elevated bond vol resets quickly.
Brazil offers some of the highest real carry in EM, with Selic at 13.75% and inflation around 4.2-4.5%. This supports BRL even without further political news, per JPM.
JPM has Brazil at 8.9x 12-month forward earnings. The next valuation regime implies 10.9x, and a structural reform scenario could take the multiple toward 13x, similar to 2016.
